text: Let's keep the promise Lesson 8 made — Unity Catalog volumes.
DBFS root had no Unity Catalog governance at all. A volume is that missing piece — governed file storage, living inside a schema, subject to the exact same grant and revoke as any table.

Create volume gives you a real path, slash Volumes, catalog, schema, volume, file — a genuine fourth level, under the catalog dot schema namespace. This is where Autoloader's incoming files belong now, instead of DBFS root.

And it's the exact same managed versus external distinction from Lesson 41, just applied to file storage instead of tables — a managed volume's location is chosen by Unity Catalog, an external one points wherever you specify.

Reading from it doesn't change at all — spark dot read and d-butils dot f-s work exactly the same. What changes is governance. Next lesson: Delta Sharing, sharing data outside this metastore entirely.
